moduleTitle: Advanced reporting insights in Tricentis Testim
learningObjectives: Use the TestOps Dashboard to monitor team activity and quality trends beyond a single test run.
Interpret metrics such as average durations and team activity alongside pass rate and failure types.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Beyond a single run: the Insights dashboard

elements.description: Insights provides branch-scoped Dashboard and Reports views with available plan features. Use their statistics to investigate test quality/activity; they do not alone certify overall application health or requirement coverage.

Compare metrics under the same relevant selection and time scope. Correlated pass-rate, duration or activity changes can guide investigation but do not prove the cause; lower activity does not by itself establish shrinking test coverage.

bulletPoints: The TestOps Dashboard is the project-health view, broader than one report or one run.
Read pass rate, failure types, durations, and activity together — not any single metric in isolation.

elements.title: TestOps Dashboard panes
items: Remote Execution Runs — passed/failed remote runs (suite/plan/scheduled/labeled), filterable to Last 24 Hours / 3 Days / 7 Days, with failure reasons and frequency.
Test Overview displays Active, Quarantine, Evaluating, Draft and Flaky categories. Flaky is retry-derived classification, not a fifth manually assigned lifecycle choice.
Duplication Level is a weekly grouping estimate; a lower score does not certify runtime correctness.
Recent Activity — an activity log with links straight to the affected test/object.
Pull Requests — Pending / Requested Changes / Approved counts; only shown when the MASTER branch is selected.

elements.text: Assigned to me leaves Duplication Level project-wide, while the remote pane switches from executions to owned-test runs. The remote pane time/filter selection does not change Test Overview or Duplication Level; do not compare these panes as though they share one denominator.

bulletPoints: Overview categories include retry-derived Flaky alongside the four lifecycle choices.
Pull Requests pane only appears when the master branch is selected.
Assigned to me changes ownership scope and the remote pane’s unit, while Duplication stays project-wide.

examPitfalls.title: Judging project health from pass rate alone
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Concluding a project is healthy purely because the pass rate looks fine, without checking duration trends or team activity.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Compare relevant metrics and effective scope before investigating causes. A stable pass rate does not certify coverage, but reduced activity alone does not prove coverage declined either.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the TestOps Dashboard provide that a single test run's result does not?

options.text: A higher-level view of project quality and team activity trends over time.
The ability to edit test steps directly.
A replacement for the CLI.
Nothing additional — it shows the same information as a single run.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's about project health over time, not one run's outcome.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The TestOps Dashboard gives a higher-level, project-wide view of quality and activity trends, letting you assess overall project health rather than reading one test run's isolated result.

optionExplanations.A: The Dashboard provides broader branch-scoped statistics and activity evidence.
optionExplanations.B: Editing test steps is not its aggregate-view role.
optionExplanations.C: A dashboard does not replace the execution runner.
optionExplanations.D: Its aggregate scope differs from one run.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should pass rate, failure types, average durations, and team activity be interpreted together rather than individually?

options.text: Because Testim only displays one metric at a time.
Because a single metric read in isolation can mask a real problem that only shows up when cross-referenced with the others.
Because they are all exactly the same underlying number.
There's no benefit — any one metric alone tells the full story.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about a stable pass rate hiding a duration regression.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A single statistic can omit relevant changes. Compare scopes and investigate evidence; correlation or activity decline does not prove the underlying cause or missing coverage.

optionExplanations.A: The view is not restricted to one isolated metric.
optionExplanations.B: Comparing appropriately scoped metrics can expose relevant changes for investigation.
optionExplanations.D: One metric does not establish the full coverage/quality picture.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which five display categories are documented in the Test Overview pane, without implying five manually assigned lifecycle choices?

options.text: Active, Quarantine, Evaluating, Draft, Flaky
Passed, Failed, Skipped, Blocked, Pending
Draft, Active, Archived, Deleted, Locked
Green, Yellow, Red, Blue, Grey

practiceQuiz.hint: Flaky is a retry-derived classification alongside the lifecycle choices.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Dashboard lists Active, Quarantine, Evaluating, Draft and Flaky. The separate lifecycle-status feature has four choices; Flaky is associated with passing after retries.

optionExplanations.A: These are the listed display categories, not five manual lifecycle choices.
optionExplanations.B: These are not the cited Overview categories.
optionExplanations.C: These do not match the documented category list.
optionExplanations.D: Colors are not the category names.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When does the Pull Requests pane appear on the TestOps Dashboard?

options.text: Always, regardless of which branch is selected.
Only when the master branch is selected.
Only on the free plan.
Only during an active CLI run.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's tied to one specific branch.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Pull Requests pane, showing Pending / Requested Changes / Approved counts, only appears on the dashboard when the master branch is the one selected.

optionExplanations.A: The pane is restricted to master in the documentation.
optionExplanations.B: Master selection is the documented branch condition.
optionExplanations.C: It is not documented as free-plan-only.
optionExplanations.D: Its availability is not tied to an active CLI run.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does the 'Assigned to me' toggle do on the TestOps Dashboard?

options.text: Deletes all data not assigned to the current user.
Filters every pane except Duplication Level down to the current user's own activity/tests.
Filters only the Duplication Level pane.
Switches to a completely different, non-filterable dashboard.

practiceQuiz.hint: One pane deliberately stays project-wide no matter what.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Ownership scoping affects applicable panes, while Duplication remains project-wide. The remote pane also switches from executions to owned-test runs; its time filters do not redefine every pane.

optionExplanations.A: Filtering does not delete other users’ data.
optionExplanations.B: Applicable ownership scope changes while Duplication remains project-wide.
optionExplanations.D: The toggle adjusts existing panes rather than launching an unrelated dashboard.

quickRecap.value: Project-wide quality/activity view, broader than a single run's result.
Pass rate + failure types + durations + team activity — not any one metric alone.
Four lifecycle choices plus retry-derived Flaky classification.
Only shown when the master branch is selected.
Ownership scope changes; remote executions become owned-test runs, and Duplication stays project-wide.
